summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for acute-on-chronic abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, following recent discontinuation of PPI and H2 blocker therapy. CT imaging showed no surgical complications but revealed new mild hydronephrosis likely due to reflux. The clinical course was consistent with bile gastritis secondary to post-gastric bypass anatomy. She was managed with bowel rest, IV then oral PPI, Carafate, and symptom control. Hypoglycemia and seizure medication needs were addressed with dextrose-containing fluids and IV levetiracetam, later transitioned to oral. Narcotics were discontinued due to limited efficacy and potential to worsen GI motility. The patient improved with medical management, advanced to a regular diet, and was discharged home with instructions to continue acid suppression, eat small frequent meals, and follow up with gastroenterology for planned outpatient endoscopy.
